title: Repair PR2947's native replay on aliased temporary roots
body:
PR2947's 59-group inventory replay errors on macOS when its entry-budget fixture compares a resolved `/private/var/...` child with an unresolved `/var/...` temporary root. This successor authenticates the archived sources and changes only that fixture's `root = Path(td)` assignment to `root = Path(td).resolve()` in memory. The one-line patch is included for review.

The archived traversal, every original assertion, production scripts, source pins, certificates and selected frontier remain unchanged. A focused Ubuntu/macOS workflow exercises this package; the historical archive stays independently inspectable.

Validation on native macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.14 and 3.14.7:

- The unmodified full replay passes all 59 groups under a canonical temporary root and errors only in the budget fixture under an explicit alias.
- The corrected full replay passes all 59 groups, zero skips, normally and under `-O` on both versions.
- Five added control groups pass in both modes and versions: forced alias/canonical controls, a disabled-budget mutant, changed/already-adapted source rejection, traversal-source drift rejection before compilation, and incomplete/failed/skipped-suite rejection.
- All 12 source rows match canonical Git objects and live input bytes; evidence code hashes, the original task card, patch application and workflow YAML syntax check pass.

Exact receipts, source hashes, commands, scope and open questions are in `research/selected-inventory-native-replay/`. Base: canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Predecessor: PR2947 head `41890b869ebbbab87262fc15d67fcad3202404a0`. This is the `portable-replay` card and a bounded prerequisite to the adoption handoff in [Discussion #2946](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2946#discussioncomment-19022542).

Hosted checks are pending at submission. Production adoption/source-pin migration, native Windows, the complete selected cold replay and independent human review remain outside this contribution. No supplier, theorem or new kappa is claimed. This manual successor has a dedicated workflow; it does not register a generic replay or claim complete transitive CI invalidation.

Credit Nick Petalas for PR2947's traversal, failure model and replay; Douglas Colkitt for the selected checker; Mihir Srivastava/PR841, yssite/PR959, Arham Tahir/PR2793, Aaron Wang and Wentao Li for the retained proof, source-closure and consumer lineage. New work by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
